key_insight: EdgeRefine improves the privacy-utility trade-off for graph learning by using Jaccard-based edge ranking and budget-aware sampling to selectively refine graph structure under edge differential privacy.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical way to preserve downstream GNN accuracy while reducing privacy leakage, making private graph analytics more deployable in sensitive domains.
method: Estimate edge-existence probabilities with Jaccard similarity.
Rank edges for noisy removal and separate true vs. false edge sampling using privacy budget ε.
Control final graph sparsity with an additional sampling rate k.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong gains over privacy-preserving baselines, including +17.8% accuracy on ACM with GAT and +19.7% on Cora with GCN at ε=2.5, plus robust reconstruction resistance.
watch_item: The approach depends on Jaccard-based edge ranking and sampling hyperparameters, so performance may vary on graphs with weak local similarity signals or different structural patterns.
paper_title: EdgeRefine: Privacy-Utility Balance for Graphs via Jaccard Sampling under Edge Differential Privacy
